QUESTION:
Will my brown garden waste bin be emptied in January?

CANDIDATE A:
No. There are no garden waste collections in December, January or February.

CANDIDATE B:
Yes. Brown bins are emptied fortnightly all year round.

RESPONSE:
Answers are based on the council's rules document. Three of these differ from my earlier notes, which had errors.

**1. Will my brown bin be emptied in January?**
No. Brown bins are emptied every two weeks from March to November only. There are no garden waste collections in December, January or February (section 4). The subscription is not reduced or refunded for the winter break. *(My notes wrongly said "throughout the year.")*

**2. Who pays to replace a stolen blue bin?**
You do. A replacement grey, blue or brown bin costs **£28, including delivery**, if it was lost, stolen or damaged by anything other than the council's crew or vehicle (section 7). Only bins damaged by the crew or vehicle are replaced free, as are food caddies. *(My notes wrongly said all bins were replaced free.)*

**3. Will they come back if I report Monday's missed grey bin on Thursday?**
No. Missed collections must be reported on the website **within two working days** of your collection day. Monday's deadline is Wednesday. The council says it cannot return for later reports, so your grey bin will be emptied on the next scheduled grey bin collection, two weeks later (section 8).

If there was a bank holiday that week, your collection day and working-day count may shift, so check the website. Until then, side waste won't be taken (section 3), so keep extra rubbish inside or at home and don't leave it on the street, to avoid a possible fixed penalty of up to £100 (section 10). *(My notes wrongly said five working days.)*

**4. By what time must bins be out?**
By **6.30 am** on your collection day, at the edge of your property next to the public highway, with lids closed. Late bins won't be collected until the next scheduled collection (section 2).
